region: Amazon basin floodplains — Peru, Brazil & Bolivia
description: A dwarf cichlid of leaf-litter shallows along the Amazon's floodplain lakes and creeks, the male recognised by his spade-shaped tail edged in red and blue. One male's territory spans several females' caves, and each female guards her own brood alone.

A German-bred line of Agassiz's dwarf cichlid in which the male's dorsal fin and spade-shaped tail are flooded with deep red. Behaviour and care are those of the wild species, including the harem breeding system.
A line-bred strain whose males wear an orange-red wash over body and fins, strongest on the face, belly and tail. It shares the wild species' biology and harem breeding.
A strain selected for the most intense red in the males' unpaired fins, the spade tail almost solid crimson with only a narrow pale base. Females remain yellow with a black band.

Named for the crest of elongated front dorsal spines that the big-mouthed male raises in display. One of the hardiest Apistogramma, it lives in small, often stagnant forest creeks and pools and keeps a harem of females, each spawning in her own cave.
A line-bred cockatoo cichlid whose males carry solid red in both the crested dorsal fin and the lyre-shaped tail. It has the wild species' hardiness and harem breeding.
A line-bred strain in which the dorsal, caudal and anal fins of males are all solid red, the most intensely coloured of the cockatoo cichlid forms. Females stay yellow with black markings.

A popular strain whose males show bright orange bands through the dorsal fin and the upper and lower edges of the lyre tail, with an orange flush on the lower flank. Care and behaviour match the wild species.

region: Paraguay–Paraná basin — Brazil, Paraguay, Bolivia & Argentina
description: A small, comparatively peaceful Apistogramma from shallow, plant-filled marshes of the Pantanal and Chaco, tolerating cooler water than most of its genus. Males have a yellow head and spread a tall "umbrella" dorsal fin in display.
A line-bred umbrella cichlid in which the blue sheen of the male spreads over the whole body as an opalescent glow behind a golden head. It keeps the cool-tolerant, peaceful nature of the wild form.

region: Río Meta basin around Villavicencio, Colombia (upper Orinoco)
description: A robust Apistogramma of clear and blackwater llanos streams, the male's tail framed by a broad red seam above a dark submarginal band. Females spawn in caves and lead their fry over the leaf litter.
A slender dwarf cichlid of shallow savanna creeks; males have red streaks across the cheeks and red-striped dorsal and tail fins over a greenish-blue body. It needs soft, acidic water to breed.

A steep-headed dwarf cichlid from Colombian llanos streams whose males flush red over the throat and lower face. Like its relative A. macmasteri it is a harem-polygynous cave spawner of soft, warm water.

region: Paraguay & Guaporé basins — Brazil, Bolivia, Paraguay & Argentina
description: A small, blue-sheened dwarf cichlid of shallow, vegetated marshes, marked by a lateral band plus a second dark stripe angling from the pectoral fin toward the belly. Males raise strongly elongated front dorsal spines when displaying.

Males of this slender species carry the most extravagantly extended front dorsal membranes in the genus, raised like a crest in display. Its two parallel dark stripes run along the flank and lower side, over leaf-litter shallows of forest streams.

region: Río Ucayali basin near Jenaro Herrera, Peru
description: Brooding females turn lemon-yellow with three bold black panda blotches on eye, flank and tail base, far more striking than the blue-grey, red-tailed males. A blackwater species that breeds only in very soft, acidic water.

region: Río Ucayali basin near Pucallpa, Peru
description: A close relative of the panda dwarf cichlid: males are pale blue-grey with a smoky tail ringed in red, and brooding females turn yellow with black blotches. It inhabits soft, tannin-stained forest streams.

Long known in the trade as Apistogramma sp. 'Inca 50', this species pairs a yellow body and black lateral band with turquoise streaks across the male's face. It lives in clear, slow forest streams of the Peruvian Andean foothills.

A blackwater dwarf cichlid whose males combine a sail-like dorsal fin with an orange-red throat and cheeks over a greenish body. It needs very soft, acidic water and is shy among roots and leaf litter.

region: Middle Rio Negro around Barcelos, Brazil
description: A blackwater specialist of the Rio Negro whose males show turquoise sheen, elongated dorsal lappets and red lines in the unpaired fins. It is among the most demanding Apistogramma, breeding only in extremely soft, acidic water.

A tiny, slender Apistogramma of Rio Negro blackwater, named for the two parallel dark bands along its flank. It lives among leaf litter in extremely soft, acidic water and is one of the smallest members of the genus.

A comparatively large, slender Apistogramma of clear and whitewater forest streams in the upper Amazon, with a dark lateral band and red-edged unpaired fins in males. Each female spawns in her own cave and guards the brood.

One of the largest Apistogramma, from Guiana Shield rivers; males grow a lyre-shaped tail and greenish iridescence over the head. It is hardier than most of its genus and tolerates near-neutral water.

region: Lower Rio Negro & Amazon near Manaus, Brazil
description: A small, slim Apistogramma of blackwater leaf-litter banks around the Rio Negro mouth; males have elongated front dorsal spines and a dark lateral band over a pale yellowish body. It is shy and best kept with very small, peaceful fishes.

region: Middle Amazon & lower Rio Negro, Brazil
description: A small, yellowish Apistogramma with a dark lateral band ending in a spot at the tail base, found in shallow, leaf-strewn forest streams. Males are only modestly larger and more colourful than females.

region: Upper Paraguay basin & Pantanal — Brazil, Bolivia & Paraguay
description: A small, peaceful Apistogramma of shallow, vegetated Pantanal waters; males show turquoise streaks on the face and a row of dark blotches along the flank. It tolerates cooler, harder water than its Amazonian relatives.

Described in 2008, this was the first Apistogramma found to mouthbrood: after spawning in a cave the female may take eggs and larvae into her mouth. Both sexes have the large heads and mouths that suit the habit.

The ram's larger, hardier cousin from the Bolivian and Brazilian lowlands, with black-tipped front dorsal spines and a red-fringed tail with trailing tips. Pairs sift sand together and spawn on a flat stone, both parents guarding the fry.

A line-bred ram in which the blue spangling has spread into a solid electric-blue body, usually with a golden forehead. It needs the same warm, soft water as the wild type but is generally less robust.
A xanthistic line-bred ram with the black pigment largely suppressed, leaving a golden body, orange-red head and faint blue spangles. Its biology and breeding match the wild species.
A line-bred ram with a genetically shortened, compressed spine that gives a rounded, balloon-like body. It keeps the German blue colouring but swims less efficiently than the wild form.

region: Coastal rivers of Guyana, Suriname & French Guiana
description: A metallic green-gold dwarf cichlid of slow, shaded Guianan creeks. In brood dress the female turns yellow with a bold black checkerboard and drives off every intruder, including the much larger male.

Named for the golden head of the male, this Nannacara has a metallic blue-green body with dark-edged scales. As in its relatives, the brooding female turns pale with a dark checkerboard and guards the fry alone.
A rare dwarf acara of the blackwater upper Rio Negro, cream-coloured with bold black bars and a red-fringed dorsal fin. Pairs share brood care and need extremely soft, acidic water.

A peaceful little acara of shallow, vegetated Amazonian backwaters, named for its steeply curved head and wearing a blue-spangled face. Pairs spawn on a cleaned leaf or stone and both parents guard the fry.

region: Paraguay & Guaporé basins — Brazil, Bolivia, Paraguay & Argentina
description: A small acara of marshy Pantanal and Chaco waters; in breeding dress the throat and breast flush deep red and a black spot shows in the front of the dorsal fin. Pairs spawn on stones and guard the brood together.

region: Rio Negro & upper Orinoco — Brazil, Colombia & Venezuela
description: A dwarf cichlid of acid blackwater creeks patterned with two rows of dark rectangular blotches; males grow lyre-shaped tails with long trailing filaments. Females spawn on leaves and guard the brood alone.

A checkerboard cichlid of the lower Amazon that lacks the lyre tail of D. filamentosus; males instead show broad, red-edged and spotted unpaired fins. It needs soft, acidic water and peaceful company.

region: Amazon basin (Peru, Ecuador, Colombia & Brazil) & Essequibo, Guyana
description: A protogynous hermaphrodite: fish mature as checkerboard-patterned females, and dominant ones later change sex into larger males covered in a red-and-blue hexagonal mosaic. It lives over sand and leaf litter in soft Amazonian streams.

region: Middle Amazon & lower Rio Negro, Brazil
description: A slender, torpedo-shaped dwarf cichlid of blackwater leaf litter, closely related to Apistogramma. Males have a pointed, lance-shaped tail; females spawn in tiny caves and guard the brood alone.
